Title: Zahid outlines 3 TVET initiatives for rural youth
Article:
SUNGAI BESAR: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has outlined three technical and vocational education and training (TVET) initiatives to produce skilled workers and entrepreneurs among rural youth.
The initiatives are the TVET Premium Career Agreement, TVET Jana Desa and Smart and Green TVET Workshops, which will be implemented in phases.
Zahid, who is also rural and regional development minister, said the TVET Premium Career Agreement would prioritise early cooperation with employers in selected programmes, including agreements on competencies, placement conditions and salary packages before trainees are recruited.
He said industry players would also be involved in curriculum development and assessments to ensure training met labour market needs.
"This approach is intended to improve job matching, ensure appropriate starting salaries and provide clearer career progression pathways for TVET graduates," he said.
He was speaking at the opening of the TVET Expo at Stadium Sungai Besar.
Zahid said the second initiative, TVET Jana Desa, aimed to produce graduates capable of establishing technical enterprises and creating jobs in their respective districts.
Fields such as agricultural machinery maintenance, pumps and cooling systems had local economic potential in areas such as Sungai Besar, he said.
"Graduates will receive business guidance, access to financing and market opportunities so that their technical skills can be developed into enterprises capable of creating jobs for local communities," he said.
Under the Smart and Green TVET Workshops initiative, workshops at TVET institutions will serve as collaborative spaces for trainees, instructors and industry players to develop practical technological solutions.
Zahid said projects being considered included machine monitoring, artificial intelligence (AI)-based automation and energy efficiency to help rural entrepreneurs increase productivity and reduce operating costs.
He said the initiatives would also complement the 2027 Budget target of placing 1,000 Bumiputera youths in high-growth sectors through Majlis Amanah Rakyat (MARA), as well as using GiatMARA wiring skills to carry out wiring repairs in 20,000 homes belonging to poor families.
"The Ministry of Rural and Regional Development, together with implementing agencies and industry partners, will also detail the institutions involved, financing mechanisms and outcome targets to ensure implementation of each initiative can be monitored and its benefits reach the intended groups," he said.
Zahid urged young people to seize TVET opportunities by choosing their fields of study seriously, developing their skills to a high level of expertise and upholding integrity at work.
He also called on parents to support their children in choosing TVET as a pathway to their futures.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysian woman rescued after falling into 10m-deep hole in Vietnam
Article:
LAM DONG, Vietnam: A 40-year-old Malaysian woman was rescued after falling into a 10m-deep hole while hiking in Da Lat, Lam Dong, on Sunday, the Vietnam News Agency reported.
The incident occurred at 5.45am in the Hon Bo mountain area of Lam Vien-Da Lat ward.
The woman, identified by her initials G.S.W., was hiking in the area when she fell into a hole about 70cm in diameter, said to be part of an abandoned mining site.
She became trapped inside the hole, and attempts by others in the hiking group to pull her out were unsuccessful. Local authorities were alerted to launch an emergency rescue operation.
Rescuers successfully brought the woman out of the hole at 7.15am and took her to Lam Dong General Hospital for emergency treatment.
Initial reports indicated she had sustained an injury to her right ankle. She received first aid before being transferred to the hospital for further treatment.
Hon Bo Mountain, near Thai Phien flower village in Da Lat, is a popular destination for hiking, cloud hunting, and photography, attracting both residents and tourists.
The mountain offers scenic views towards Da Lat's centre, particularly in the early morning. However, spontaneous hiking and sightseeing in the area can pose safety risks, especially for visitors unfamiliar with the local terrain.
Authorities advised visitors to exercise caution when exploring mountainous areas and to avoid hiking independently in locations where the terrain and potential hazards are unfamiliar.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Penang on alert for floods, landslides after fatal tragedy
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Penang authorities have advised residents to remain alert for flash floods and landslides following overnight rain and high tides.
State Infrastructure Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said the Malaysian Meteorological Department had forecast rain from Oct 24 to 26.
"With continuous heavy rain and high tide levels, flash floods will occur. We advise everyone to be on alert.
"Slopes are particularly vulnerable after prolonged heavy rain as the soil could loosen, increasing the risk of landslides," he said.
He said agencies, including the Penang Island City Council (MBPP) and the Public Works Department (PWD), would remain on alert.
This follows the death of a
73-year-old
man in a landslide behind his house in Taman Seri Rambai, Paya Terubong, today.
Meanwhile, state Local Government Committee chairman Jason H'ng said several areas across Penang reported fallen trees following the overnight downpour.
The affected locations included Lorong Gangsa, Lebuh Bukit Jambul, Lebuh Halia 1, Jalan Mayang Pasir near Bayan Baru market, Lintang Bukit Jambul, the Macallum open field, Taman Sri Nibong, Lengkok Hijau, Gertak Sanggul, Jalan Paya Terubong, the Road Transport Department office in Batu Uban and Golden Triangle 2.
Motorists are advised to exercise caution, particularly on hilly roads where fallen trees, slippery surfaces and unstable slopes could pose hazards.
MBPP mayor Datuk A. Rajendran said 14 incidents involving fallen trees and broken branches had been reported, comprising 13 fallen trees and one broken branch.
Heavy rain and high tides also caused flooding and water accumulation at 10 locations across the island's northeast and southwest districts.
Rajendran said rainfall recorded between 1am and 11am reached 117mm at the Kolam Bersih station and 97.5mm at the Kolam Air Itam station.
Flooding in the northeast district was attributed to prolonged heavy rain, high tides and the overflowing of Sungai Pinang, while low-lying terrain contributed to flooding in the southwest district.
The affected locations in the northeast included Lintang P. Ramlee, Jalan P. Ramlee, Jalan Kampung Relau, Jalan Patani, Lilitan Stadium, Kampung Masjid Hashim Yahya and Lorong Kulit, where water levels reached about 50cm.
In the southwest district, flooding was reported at Kampung Sulup, Kampung Masjid and Kampung Paya, with water levels reaching about 30cm.
Immediate measures included clearing drainage systems in affected areas, while the long-term solution involved the Drainage and Irrigation Department's Sungai Pinang flood mitigation project.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 27 schools in Tebedu to close tomorrow as API exceeds 200
Article:
KUCHING: A total of 27 schools in Tebedu will be temporarily closed tomorrow after the Air Pollutant Index (API) exceeded 200, with home-based teaching and learning (PdPR) activated.
The Sarawak Education Department said the closure involves one secondary school and 26 primary schools, based on ongoing monitoring and API readings recorded at 2pm today.
The decision also took into account Malaysian Meteorological Department reports on haze conditions across the state.
The department said PdPR implementation aligns with the Education Ministry Circular No. 8/2016 on teaching and learning management guidelines during disasters.
Teachers and implementation support staff are also permitted to work from home throughout the temporary closure.
The department said the closure directive applies to all primary and secondary schools in districts that record API readings exceeding 200 after the issuance of the statement.
However, face-to-face classes will continue for Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) candidates with strict adherence to face mask guidelines.
The measure complies with Circular No. 1/2005 on preparations for haze threats during examinations (Operasi Topeng) and the Special Operations Guidelines: Disaster and Crisis Management During Examinations (Revised Edition) 2026.
For schools located near districts recording API readings above 200, headmasters and principals may consider implementing PdPR based on student safety and health.
If API readings show a downward trend below the 200 threshold, school administrators may initiate preparations to reopen.
Tebedu, located in Serian Division, is the closest district to the Malaysia-Indonesia border.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Takiyuddin: Bersatu leaders invited to PN meeting tonight
Article:
KOTA BARU: The status of Perikatan Nasional's (PN) case against the Registrar of Societies (RoS) over its
suspension
and the coalition's preparations for the Melaka state election will be the main agenda at a meeting in Kuala Lumpur tonight.
PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said Bersatu leaders had been invited to the meeting at the Pas headquarters tonight.
However, the Pas secretary-general said it was up to Bersatu leaders to decide whether to attend."
On the
seven seats
allocated to PN for the upcoming Melaka polls, Takiyuddin said they would be distributed among the coalition's component parties.
He said Bersatu would not be included in the allocation as the party had decided to use its own logo in the election.
The five PN component parties are Pas, Gerakan, the Malaysian Indian People's Party (MIPP), Parti Gerakan Rakyat Malaysia and Pejuang.
Takiyuddin, the Kota Baru member of parliament, said the distribution of the seven seats would also be discussed at the meeting, adding that the number of seats available was limited.
He said the coalition would have to work out an appropriate distribution among the parties involved.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysian vessel took delivery of 1.16 tonnes of drugs in Andaman Sea
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian vessel intercepted by Indonesian authorities with 1.16 tonnes of ketamine had taken delivery of the drugs from a foreign mothership in the Andaman Sea.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the foreign mothership was believed to be registered in a country within the Golden Triangle region.
"Based on information received from the Indonesian National Police (Polri), the drugs were loaded through a ship-to-ship transfer in the Andaman Sea," he told the New Straits Times.
A ship-to-ship transfer involves moving cargo directly between two vessels at sea without either having to dock at a port.
Such transfers are commonly used for legitimate commercial purposes, including moving oil and other cargo, but can also be exploited by drug syndicates to avoid port inspections.
Hussein said that while preliminary investigations indicated the foreign mothership had transferred the drugs to the Malaysian-registered MT Global 168, Bukit Aman was looking at the case from all angles.
He said police were investigating the case under Section 34 of the Dangerous Drugs Act for facilitating drug offences committed outside Malaysia, to establish whether there were any Malaysian links to the shipment.
The provision allows action to be taken against anyone who, while in Malaysia, assists or undertakes preparatory acts connected to drug offences overseas.
Hussein said Bukit Aman was also working with its Indonesian counterparts, who intercepted the vessel, which was sailing under the Mongolian flag, in waters off Tanjung Balai Asahan, Indonesia, on Oct 20.
On the vessel's movements, Hussein said MT Global 168 departed Pasir Gudang, Johor, in early October before stopping at Port Klang to refuel.
It then headed towards the Andaman Sea, with its Automatic Identification System (AIS) pinging its location off Aceh on Oct 15.
Between Oct 16 and 18, however, the vessel made unusual circular movements off Thailand's west coast, and its AIS was switched off for three days.
After the AIS was switched back on, the vessel was tracked in Indonesian waters heading towards Port Klang before it was intercepted by Polri, customs officials, the National Narcotics Agency and maritime police.
Indonesian authorities found 58 sacks containing 1,160 packages of ketamine hydrochloride weighing a total of 1.16 tonnes.
The drugs have an estimated street value of 3.48 trillion rupiah (US$192.64 million).
Yesterday, Hussein revealed that the vessel belonged to a company registered in Malaysia with an office address in Johor Baru.
He said the company had two Malaysian directors, aged in their 40s and 50s, neither of whom had previous criminal records.
Both directors will be called in to assist investigations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PH's decades-long bond must endure, says Saifuddin
Article:
MELAKA: Pakatan Harapan was built on decades of camaraderie that must be upheld by all component parties, candidates and election machinery.
PH secretary-general Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the coalition's strength rested not only on shared political goals but also on mutual trust, respect and loyalty.
He said the bond dated back to September 1998 and had endured numerous challenges before PH formed the federal government.
"This is not a friendship of two or three years. This is a story of camaraderie that began in September 1998 and continues to this day.
"Pakatan Harapan is a political coalition we must take pride in because it is bound by camaraderie. This is an invaluable political virtue," he said.
He was speaking at the Melaka PH candidate announcement and election machinery launch at the Hang Jebat Stadium compound yesterday.
Saifuddin said he had witnessed the opposition movement evolve from Barisan Alternatif to Pakatan Rakyat and eventually PH.
He said the coalition had endured a long political journey through the 1999, 2004, 2008, 2013, 2018 and 2022 general elections before securing the mandate to govern the country.
"Whatever political trials may come, as long as we hold fast to these values, PH is a coalition that will endure," he said.
Saifuddin said a coalition's real test was not merely winning elections, but also managing the people's trust once in power.
He said PH must use its mandate to ensure political stability, economic prosperity and public welfare, supported by good governance and prudent financial management without wastage, leakages or corruption.
He also called for closer cooperation among component parties during elections, saying PKR's machinery must work hard to help DAP candidates win in their constituencies, with DAP and Amanah providing the same support to PKR candidates.
"When PKR contests, regardless of who the candidate is in that area, DAP and Amanah must work as though their own candidates are contesting," he said.
Saifuddin said such solidarity would strengthen PH's electoral performance if all component parties put their shared interests first.
Recalling his early days in politics, he said he had accompanied Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu on political ceramah tours during semester breaks, including in Pekan, Pahang, and Kuala Pilah, Negri Sembilan.
They handled the public address system and lighting themselves and sold cassette tapes to cover travel expenses, he said, describing the sacrifices made in building the political movement more than 30 years ago.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka election: 7 new PKR faces can deliver surprises, says Adam Adli
Article:
AYER KEROH: PKR has named seven new candidates for the Melaka election to strengthen the party's position in the state.
They will join two "old hands" in Wanita PKR information chief Datuk Ginie Lim Siew Lin in the Machap Jaya seat and Tangga Batu PKR Youth chief Farzana Hayani Mohd Nasir in Klebang.
Acting state PKR chairman Adam Adli Abd Halim said the new faces being fielded bring different experiences and responsibilities, offering renewed hope for the party.
He said they were "winnable candidates" capable of challenging Barisan Nasional.
He said all candidates must work hard to earn voters' trust, as their chances of winning does not solely depend on popularity or a candidate's personal strengths.
Instead, he said, community ties, the strength of the party machinery and the effectiveness of the agenda being presented were among the key factors in determining voter support.
"Everyone contests an election to win. However, victory depends not only on name recognition or personal strengths, but also on ties with the community, an effective campaign machinery and the agenda being presented to the voters.
"Most importantly, they must make the interests of the community and voters their top priority," he said at the Madani Kita with the Ayer Keroh Community @ Hang Tuah Jaya Parliamentary Constituency programme at the Sungai Putat people's housing project here today.
Present were Community Communications Department director-general Mohd Hisyamuddin Ghazali and former Ayer Keroh assemblyman Kerk Chee Yee.
Adam Adli said PKR recognises that much more needs to be done to convince voters of the party's capabilities, including translating its agenda of change and reform at the federal level into tangible benefits for the people of Melaka.
He said the party's candidates must ensure that the principles of good governance and accountability to the people are reflected in their approach and work at the local level.
He also reminded candidates to maintain good conduct and personal integrity throughout the campaign period.
On Pakatan Harapan's decision to contest only 21 of the 28 state seats, the Hang Tuah Jaya member of parliament said this was made based on several considerations, including the party's strength, the readiness of its election machinery and its chances of winning.
He said PH needed to optimise its available resources by focusing on constituencies where its campaign operations and election machinery are better prepared.
However, he did not rule out changes in the remaining seven seats.
"We still have six days before nomination day, and many things can happen. I am confident that no seat will be left uncontested.
"We have never ruled out the possibility of negotiations and will see over the next few days what other decisions can be made," he said.
Among the new faces being fielded are the prime minister's political secretary, Datuk Azman Abidin, in the Paya Rumput seat, as well as Esma Eazreen Husin in Rim, and Mohd Khuzaire Mohd Kamal Kannan in Rembia.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: IGP conferred Professor of Practice title
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail was conferred the title of Professor of Practice by Spectrum International University College (SIUC).
The title was presented to Khalid by SIUC chairman Tan Sri Professor Emeritus Datuk Dr Mohamed Salleh Mohamed Yasin during the university's 26th convocation at the JW Marriott Hotel Putrajaya.
Khalid described the accolade as a significant milestone and an opportunity to bridge academic concepts with the realities of public service.
"During my tenure with the police force, I learned that true leadership is defined by service to others, not by rank.
"I look forward to sharing my insights to help develop future leaders and guide them as they move from the classroom to the professional world," he said.
Addressing the 2026 graduating class, Khalid said effective leadership required taking responsibility, making tough choices and prioritising integrity over authority.
"In public service, trust is our most valuable asset. We cannot demand or legislate trust; we must earn it through consistent action and strong character.
"While academic qualifications open doors, character ultimately determines trustworthiness."
Khalid cautioned graduates against ethical compromises, the temptation of quick financial gains and involvement in illegal activities, including cybercrime.
"Never let greed, peer pressure, or the promise of quick money jeopardise your future.
"Before making important decisions, ask whether the reward is worth risking your freedom, reputation, and others' trust.
"Choose honesty and responsibility, even when it is difficult."
He urged graduates to uphold three core principles throughout their careers: pursuing excellence, safeguarding personal integrity and serving the community.
"Malaysia needs not only skilled professionals, but also trustworthy leaders, responsible entrepreneurs, and dedicated citizens.
"Let us work for a Malaysia where opportunities are based on merit, integrity is central, and success is measured by our ability to uplift others."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Picking up friends' claim no defence for illegal airport drivers
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Drivers caught ferrying passengers illegally at Penang International Airport often claimed they were picking up friends or acquaintances, but this did not deter Road Transport Department (RTD) enforcement action.
The department inspected 12 vehicles during an operation that began at 8am, issuing six notices involving three vehicles found carrying passengers without valid permits.
Penang RTD director Zulkifly Ismail said the operation was conducted following intelligence gathering and public complaints about illegal taxi activities at tourist spots and major entry points in Penang.
"Among the excuses given by the drivers was that they were there to pick up friends or acquaintances.
"This is a common excuse we receive," he said at the airport.
The drivers were investigated under Section 16 of the Land Public Transport Act 2010 for carrying passengers without valid permits.
From Jan 1 to Oct 24, RTD Penang inspected 1,056 vehicles suspected of operating without valid permits.
Of these, 496 vehicles were subjected to enforcement action, with 519 notices issued.
Zulkifly said illegal passenger transport services were taken seriously as they could jeopardise passenger safety and create unfair competition for legitimate operators.
He added that all cases detected so far involved local drivers, with no foreign drivers arrested for the offence.
RTD Penang would continue its monitoring and enforcement operations to ensure commercial passenger transport operators complied with licensing and permit requirements, he said.
"Passenger safety cannot be compromised.
"We encourage the public to channel information on suspected illegal transport activities through our official channels," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fitch maintains Ukraine at 'CCC', expects war to extend into 2027
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Global credit ratings agency Fitch on Friday maintained Ukraine's long-term foreign-currency rating at "CCC", deep in speculative territory, saying it expects the country's ongoing war with Russia to drag into 2027.
The US is pushing to end the 4-1/2-year-old war that has escalated this year as Russia intensified aerial attacks and Ukraine targeted Russia's oil and gas sector. Peace negotiators are meeting next month for new talks
Ukraine's sovereign ratings remain in speculative territory as the country relies heavily on foreign financial assistance to fund budget deficits and support the economy while continuing to defend against Russia's invasion
Fitch said its rating reflects "substantial" credit risk given the war and its effects, balanced by a manageable near-term debt service profile, an improved level of foreign exchange reserves, and significant support from partners
Ukraine is likely to continue running large fiscal deficits due to high wartime spending and weak domestic revenue generation, while its economy is expected to contract marginally in 2026 before returning to growth of 0.2 per cent in 2027, it added
Fitch typically does not assign outlooks to sovereigns with a rating of "CCC+" or below
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Protesters clash with police over India's mega-dam project near China
Article:
NEW DELHI: Indian protesters angry over a proposed Himalayan mega-dam, intended to counter an upstream Chinese hydropower project, have clashed with police and torched buildings, officials said.
The violence in northeastern Arunachal Pradesh state erupted late on Friday during protests against the proposed 11,200-megawatt Siang Upper Multipurpose Project of state-run hydropower company NHPC, Chief Minister Pema Khandu told reporters on Saturday.
"The mob destroyed a lot of properties, police station, the NHPC office was vandalised, several elected representatives' homes were ransacked," Khandu told reporters.
Around 40 police personnel were injured by stones thrown by protesters, who also vandalised the NHPC's offices. Police fired tear gas canisters to disperse the crowd.
Khandu urged opponents of the project to engage with the government.
"Question us, have dialogue with us, instead of violence," Khandu said.
India says the proposed dam is needed to counter China's US$167-billion Yaxia project, a likely record-breaking hydropower scheme upstream in Tibet.
New Delhi fears the Chinese project could affect water flows downstream, and says the proposed Indian dam would create a vast reservoir to store water and help maintain flows into the Brahmaputra river.
Beijing has said its project will have no "negative impact" downstream.
China claims Arunachal Pradesh as part of southern Tibet. India says the state is an integral part of its territory.
India's proposed dam, which would be by far its largest hydropower project, has drawn fierce opposition from local communities who fear the loss of their homes and land.
The project underscores tensions between the two most populous countries, which share a disputed Himalayan border patrolled by tens of thousands of troops.
India's foreign ministry said on Friday the two sides remained in regular contact to manage border tensions, after a top Indian border police official Shatrujeet Kapur reported "face offs" between Indian and Chinese forces.
"The situation in the India-China border areas gets disturbed from time to time when Chinese forces diverge from established patrolling patterns," foreign ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal told reporters in New Delhi.
"Both sides continue to use existing diplomatic and military mechanisms to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation."--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Binastra tipped for 21pct earnings growth, gets  "Buy" call
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Maybank Investment Bank Bhd (Maybank IB) has initiated coverage on Binastra Corp Bhd with a "Buy" call and a target price of RM3.40.
The firm forecasted a three-year forward earnings compound annual growth rate of 21 per cent for the company, assuming annual job wins of RM2.5 billion.
"In our view, Binastra's net cash balance sheet position also gives it the valuable option to raise its dividend payout ratio from more than 50 per cent currently," it said in a note.
"As the executive directors do not receive salaries but are incentivised by dividends as a reward, we believe high dividend payouts are sustainable, which would also benefit minority shareholders."
The firm noted that Binastra Operating Franchise has more than 40 years of construction experience and has completed 189 projects with a cumulative revenue of more than RM12 billion.
Its current outstanding order book stands at RM6.7 billion over 30 ongoing projects nationwide.
It added that Binastra evolved from a predominantly Klang Valley high-rise residential property contractor into a multi-segment construction group.
"Its current portfolio includes data centres, renewable energy infrastructure, sewage treatment plants and specialised engineering. The latter segments account for 30 per cent of its outstanding order book, but Binastra aims to raise this percentage to 40-50 per cent," it added.
Although these segments yield lower margins, the firm views them favourably as they are turned around quicker than high-rise residential property and will contribute to group net profit faster.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: JS-SEZ to drive Johor industrial demand, lift AME Reit prospects
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) is bound to be a supportive tailwind for industrial demand in Johor that will benefit AME Real Estate Investment Trust (Reit), said RHB Research.
The firm said that it remains positive on AME Reit's prospects supported by the JS-SEZ as well as its resilient portfolio fundamentals, strong tenant retention and embedded rental mark-to-market opportunities.
"With portfolio occupancy at 100 per cent, near-term income visibility remains strong, while the gap between recent achieved rents of RM2.50 per sq ft and existing passing rents of RM1.80–1.90/sq ft provides further rental mark-to-market opportunities as leases progressively expire," it said in a note.
On inorganic growth, the firm targets RM100 million in annual acquisitions, supported by its established industrial ecosystem and third-party opportunities.
"While AME Reit's borrowings remain at a fully floating rate, we estimate a 25 basis point rate hike would have a manageable 1.7 per cent impact on its earnings in FY28."
AME Reit's core earnings of RM23.2 million for the first half of financial year 2027 (FY27) accounted for 47 per cent of RHB Research's full-year forecasts and 50 per cent of consensus'.
The firm maintained its "Buy" call on the stock with a lower target price of RM1.92, following an adjustment to its risk-free rate assumption to 4.0 per cent to reflect the recent rise in Malaysian government securities yields.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Petronas upstream capex rises 19pct, bolstering oil and gas outlook
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's oil and gas sector will be supported by continued upstream investment, offshore activity and recurring contact income amid rising concerns on the renewed Middle East tensions that pushed Brent crude price back above the US$100 per barrel (bbl) level.
RHB Research noted that Petroliam Nasional Bhd's (Petronas) capital expenditure (capex) of RM41.4 billion in the first half of 2026 (1H26) looked substantial, but focus should be on the upstream segment.
It said Petronas' capital investments in 1H26 were skewed by downstream business, which accounted for RM26 billion or 63 per cent of the total, driven by additional capital injection into the Pengerang Refining Company and Pengerang Petrochemical joint venture.
"Hence, we believe upstream capex is the more relevant indicator, rising 19 per cent year-on-year to RM8.7 billion in 1H26. Overall, we believe the growth in upstream investment remains the key positive takeaway for Malaysia's oil and gas sector," it said in a note.
The firm kept its Brent crude price assumption at US$89/bbl and US$72/bbl for 2026 and 2027, respectively, reflecting its expectation for the current geopolitical risk premium to eventually moderate.
RHB Research added that the higher oil price environment should provide a favourable backdrop for upstream activity, while elevated freight rates offer potential upside for shipping companies like MISC Bhd.
"Meanwhile, recurring contract income, ongoing offshore activity, and healthy orderbook visibility should underpin earnings resilience across the sector.
"Overall, we remain constructive on the sector, with upstream activity, contracted cash flows, and tanker-market strength providing key earnings support," it said.
The firm maintained its "Overweight" call on the sector with MISC and Dialog Group Bhd as top picks.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Warisan seeks 26 seats in next general election, says Shafie
Article:
SANDAKAN: Warisan is targeting 26 parliamentary seats in the next general election in cooperation with its coalition partners, said party president Datuk Seri Mohd Shafie Apdal.
"God willing, we want 26 seats and partner parties to ensure we achieve success and amplify Sabah's voice," he said when officiating the Warisan annual general assembly at Dewan Hakka here today.
Also present were Warisan deputy president Datuk Darell Leiking, Parti Kesejahteraan Demokratik Masyarakat (KDM) president Priscella Peter and Parti Solidariti Tanah Airku (Star) acting deputy president Datuk Lawrence Gimbang.
Sabah has 25 parliamentary seats, while Labuan has one, out of the 222 seats nationwide.
Shafie said the priority was to field winnable candidates, while seat allocations should reflect each party's strength.
"There is no point fielding candidates who cannot win. We must identify those who can," he said, adding that discussions on seat allocations were premature.
He said political leaders must engage with grassroots communities and listen to their concerns rather than rely on popularity on social media.
Drawing on more than 30 years in politics, Shafie said parties could complement one another's strengths and weaknesses, stressing that cooperation should not benefit only one side.
"I have worked with many parties and made mistakes that we must learn from. We learn from history. Without the voices and parties here, cooperation at the federal level would not materialise," he said.
He said the presence of KDM and Star leaders at the assembly reflected cooperation ahead of the general election.
Shafie said the collaboration was based on sincerity and shared strengths to ensure Sabah's voice was effectively represented at the federal level.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Cops identify people linked to ketamine tanker, arrests expected
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police have identified several people and companies linked to a tanker suspected of involvement in drug trafficking and are working to locate them for arrest, Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said.
"We have identified the people. We are trying to locate their whereabouts. The companies and those involved are also in our knowledge.
"Arrests will be made as soon as possible, potentially today or tomorrow," he said after the Spectrum International University College 26th convocation.
Yesterday, Indonesian authorities seized the tanker over the suspected smuggling of
1.16 tonnes of ketamine
.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the MT Global 168 was owned by a Johor Baru-based company with two Malaysian directors in their 40s and 50s.
He said both directors had no previous criminal records and would be called in to assist investigations.
Khalid said preliminary investigations showed that the vessel, which is registered in Mongolia, had originated from Johor Baru and was sailing towards the Andaman Sea.
He said illicit activities, including mid-sea transfers, could have taken place.
"There may have been things that occurred beyond our knowledge, such as a ship-to-ship transfer while the vessel was in international waters."
Khalid said Bukit Aman maintained close working relationships with its Asean counterparts, including Indonesia and Laos, as well as international law enforcement partners.
"Malaysian police are now working in close coordination with their Indonesian counterparts to facilitate joint investigations and bring those involved to justice."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Philippines probes Thomas Markle laptop over child abuse images as Meghan speaks out
Article:
MANILA: Philippine police are investigating a laptop found alongside images of child abuse at the former home of Meghan Markle's estranged father, with "full results" expected in a week, the country's interior minister told AFP.
Thomas Markle, whose daughter is married to Britain's Prince Harry, had been living in Cebu in the Philippines until reportedly returning to the United States earlier this year.
Philippine interior minister Jonvic Remulla told AFP the country planned to take "appropriate legal actions" against Markle – who has denied all claims of alleged offending – if sufficient evidence was found.
"The Philippine National Police (PNP), upon the reports of the son, inspected the former home of a certain Mr. Thomas Markle," Remulla said in a text message sent late Saturday. "Found were a trove of child pornography materials as well as a laptop."
"The laptop is currently going under forensic investigation and we will have the full results in one week," Remulla said.
"The PNP will coordinate with their counterparts to locate and take appropriate legal actions against Mr. Markle if found that there is sufficient evidence to charge him."
British tabloid the Sun first reported last week that Markle's son, Thomas Markle Jr., had discovered the child abuse images while going through boxes found in his father's former home.
On Friday, Meghan Markle said she was "deeply distressed" by accusations her father had possessed images of child abuse, adding she had blocked contact between him and her children over previous "troubling and disturbing" allegations.
After the reports, Meghan said that in 2018 she had seen a letter sent to London's Metropolitan Police and Royalty and Specialist Protection making similar accusations.
"It made troubling and disturbing allegations against my father, and I was given assurances that these were being investigated," she said in a statement.
London's Metropolitan police said it had passed on the information to the royal couple but did not share it with other law enforcement agencies.
Meghan Markle and Prince Harry left Britain and quit royal duties in 2020 amid a bitter royal family feud.
They made an unexpected return with their children to live in the United Kingdom in August.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MCA to decide in two days if it will still contest Melaka polls
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: MCA will hold an emergency meeting within the next two days to decide whether it will contest the upcoming Melaka election after walking out of Barisan Nasional's candidate unveiling last night.
Party president Datuk Seri Wee Ka Siong said MCA was
caught off guard
when BN unveiled its candidates after the party had been told that only the coalition's election machinery would be launched yesterday.
"On Thursday, MCA was told that we would be given two seats — both of which we won in the last election. In 2021, we contested seven seats," Wee told the New Straits Times.
"We voiced our objections and were told that the matter would be discussed."
Wee said he and other MCA leaders turned up at the launch of BN's election machinery in Melaka last night only to discover that the coalition would also be unveiling its candidates.
"MCA has not even submitted the names of our candidates, and BN wants to name them.
"Where is the courtesy? We did not have this problem in Johor and Negri Sembilan."
Wee said if state BN leaders could push component parties around, it raised questions about the role of component party presidents.
"We will meet within the next couple of days and decide whether we are still going to contest the election."
Earlier today, BN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said negotiations on
MCA's candidate list
for the Melaka election remain open.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tropical Storm Champi nears China after battering Taiwan, Japan
Article:
TAIPEI: A powerful storm swept towards China on Saturday after battering Taiwan and Japan's southernmost islands, knocking out power to thousands of households and forcing the cancellation of hundreds of flights.
Typhoon Champi was downgraded to a tropical storm as its wind speed dropped to 102km per hour, according to the latest update from the Joint Typhoon Warning Center.
Taiwanese authorities evacuated more than 5,000 people from their homes ahead of the storm, which toppled trees, brought down power lines and triggered brief flooding.
One person was killed and more than 600 injured since Thursday, when the government began issuing warnings about the typhoon.
Power has been restored to more than 90 per cent of over 340,000 affected households, after the storm unleashed fierce winds and heavy rain over swathes of Taiwan.
Most shops across northern and central Taiwan were closed for a second day, as the typhoon moved away from the island's northeast and headed north towards China.
"Although the typhoon is gradually departing, we would like to remind the public that coastal areas will still experience swells and strong wind gusts," the Central Weather Administration's Wuu Woan-hwa said at a briefing.
Champi is the latest in a busy Pacific storm season turbocharged by the El Nino weather phenomenon that has caused unprecedented warming in the equatorial Pacific.
The storm was briefly a super typhoon as it crossed the ocean in recent days, with reported maximum sustained wind speeds of nearly 300kph.
Its intensity weakened overnight as it made a loop off Taiwan's northeastern county of Yilan, where it has dumped at least 65cm of rain since Thursday, the forecaster said.
Martha Wang said she was afraid of being "blown away" by the wind as she rode her scooter across a bridge in New Taipei City on Saturday morning.
"I was really scared because I was on the bridge. My scooter was shaking," the 55-year-old secretary told AFP.
William Yu, however, was unfazed by the storm, saying it "wasn't any stronger than other typhoons."
"I went to the convenience store to eat yesterday (evening) and everything was fine," the 55-year-old librarian said.
- HEADING FOR CHINA -
Authorities in China warned of "strong winds and heavy rain" as Champi approaches the country's east coast, state broadcaster CCTV said.
Some train services have been suspended and tens of thousands evacuated from their homes in Shanghai.
"Some areas of Jiangsu, Shanghai, Zhejiang, and other regions are expected to experience heavy to torrential rainfall," it said.
Hundreds of flights have been cancelled in the region, including in Japan's southernmost prefecture of Okinawa where the government said two people were injured in the typhoon.
Tourists on Ishigaki island waited for flights to resume so they could return home.
"We hope it's our last day," Eva Malek, 49, from Poland told AFP.
"It's not easy to have information. We were not aware of the situation and didn't expect something like this to happen. When the typhoon arrived we didn't think it would be that strong."
The United Nations said Wednesday that the El Nino system gripping the planet is heading off the charts and that countries should take urgent action to prepare for the worst.
El Nino is expected to peak in December, but the human impact is set to last into 2027 and beyond.
The warming phase of a natural climate cycle, El Nino temporarily raises sea temperatures in the tropical Pacific, triggering changes in weather that can increase the risk of drought and flooding and exacerbate human-caused global warming.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 90,000 Form Six students to benefit from RM2,500 allowance from next year
Article:
NIBONG TEBAL: Form Six students will receive a total RM2,500 living allowance from next year, with payments disbursed in stages over three semesters.
Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the assistance would be channelled during the first semester after student registration was completed.
She said the allowance was part of the 2027 Budget, with each eligible student receiving the total amount throughout their three-semester pre-university programme.
"Once registration for all Form Six students is completed, we will provide the assistance during their first semester.
"They will start receiving the allowance in the first semester next year," she told reporters after officiating the closing ceremony of the Jelajah Negaraku: Aku Kasih Malaysia programme at Taman Widuri today.
Fadhlina, who is also the Nibong Tebal member of parliament, said the initiative reflected the government's commitment to providing students with better support for their studies.
She said the assistance was also expected to improve the quality of Form Six education, particularly the performance of students sitting for the Sijil Tinggi Persekolahan Malaysia (STPM) examination.
"We are pleased with the Budget announcement as one of our aspirations is to ensure Form Six students receive adequate support in their studies and to improve the quality of STPM," she said.
Under the 2027 Budget, the government agreed to provide the RM2,500 living allowance to about 90,000
Form Six students
nationwide.
Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had said the initiative was aimed at safeguarding the welfare of pre-university students.
The allowance also brings financial assistance for Form Six students in line with the rate received by matriculation students, supporting greater equity in financial aid for pre-university education.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Wan Rosdy: ECRL to open new doors for east coast entrepreneurs
Article:
KUANTAN: East coast entrepreneurs must prepare to seize economic opportunities when the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) begins operations in December.
National Entrepreneur and Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) Development Council special adviser Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail said the ECRL would offer more than just transport connectivity, with the potential to stimulate economic activity, tourism, logistics and trade across Pahang, Terengganu and Kelantan.
The ECRL, which will connect Kota Baru to the Gombak Integrated Transport Terminal via Kelantan, Terengganu, Pahang and Selangor, is scheduled to begin operations on Dec 12.
Wan Rosdy said the rail link would open up new opportunities for entrepreneurs to reach more customers, strengthen supply chains and expand their businesses.
"It will create opportunities for MSMEs in various sectors, including food and beverage, accommodation, transportation, goods supply and support services.
"I want entrepreneurs to start preparing early, improve their service quality and ensure their products meet market demand. They must use business gatherings as platforms to explore potential collaborations.
"Stronger cooperation in marketing, product distribution, raw material supply and market expansion could create more opportunities for local businesses to grow," he told reporters after attending a dialogue with east coast MSME entrepreneurs at the Youth and Sports Complex here today.
Wan Rosdy, who is also Pahang menteri besar, said MSMEs must not merely be spectators to this major connectivity development but should position themselves to benefit from it and drive economic growth in the east coast region.
Meanwhile, he said the business landscape was changing rapidly, with rising operating costs, global economic uncertainties, supply chain shifts and evolving consumer demands requiring entrepreneurs to become more efficient and better prepared for competition.
"I urge entrepreneurs not to fear change, particularly when it comes to adopting technology. For example, artificial intelligence can help with marketing, customer service, sales analysis and operational management," he said.
On the dialogue, Wan Rosdy said it provided an opportunity to engage directly with entrepreneurs and hear first-hand about their experiences and challenges.
"I want to hear what assistance they need, the challenges they face and what improvements the government and relevant agencies can make. We do not want assistance to be provided without taking into account the actual needs of its recipients.
"We are here not to find fault with anyone, but to find solutions. Every initiative must deliver clear benefits to entrepreneurs," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'I felt my arm swelling': GOF corporal injured in drug suspect's escape bid
Article:
PASIR MAS: A routine patrol yesterday turned into a frightening encounter for a 41-year-old General Operations Force corporal when a suspected drug syndicate member rammed his vehicle in an attempt to evade arrest.
The corporal, who has served in the police force for 14 years, said he and three colleagues from the GOF's Ninth Battalion were patrolling Jalan Kedai Lama in Rantau Panjang at about 2pm when they spotted a suspicious car.
"We tried to overtake the Toyota Corolla Altis, but the driver suddenly rammed our vehicle.
"Both vehicles sustained severe damage to their front sections," he said.
Despite the impact, the corporal and his colleagues immediately got out of their vehicle and approached the suspect's car.
They managed to pull the 35-year-old
suspect
out before he could flee.
However, the incident left the corporal with a fractured right arm, an injury he initially did not realise was serious.
"About half an hour after the incident, I started feeling swelling in my right arm.
"I was then taken to hospital, where doctors confirmed that my arm was fractured," he said.
His right arm was put in a cast yesterday evening, and he was discharged from Lati Hospital last night.
The father of a two-year-old daughter said this was the first time he had been involved in such an incident in his nine years serving with the GOF.
Despite the painful experience, he remained focused on his duties, describing the incident as an unexpected risk that came with police work.
The 35-year-old suspect was arrested and remanded for four days from today.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: IGP: CID ordered to probe Noorizwan's death after unusual injuries found
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Criminal Investigation Department (CID) has been ordered to investigate the death of detainee Noorizwan Zulkefly, 42, at the Cheras police headquarters following the discovery of several unusual injuries on his body.
Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said police were awaiting the full laboratory report to establish the cause of death.
"From what we have seen, there are several unusual injuries that require attention, and I have asked the CID, especially its director Datuk M. Kumar, to investigate the matter as soon as possible," he said after the Spectrum International University College convocation ceremony today.
​Khalid added that he had instructed the CID to issue public updates on the progress of the investigation.
Yesterday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim called for a thorough, transparent and uncompromising investigation into Noorizwan's death in police custody.
Anwar also
expressed condolences
to the family, acknowledging their grief and anxiety as they sought answers about the circumstances surrounding his death.
Noorizwan's family had submitted a memorandum to Anwar at his house in Bandar Sungai Long yesterday, appealing for his intervention in the case.
The family, accompanied by Lawyers for Liberty, called for immediate action and justice following his death while in detention at the Cheras district police headquarters, where he had been held since Sept 19.
Noorizwan died at Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz on Oct 1 after being taken there for treatment the previous day.
His preliminary post-mortem report stated that he had sustained multiple bodily injuries.
The family has called for a thorough investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding his death.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: UDA unveils show unit for new Residensi Mutiara housing project
Article:
JOHOR BARU: UDA Holdings Bhd has unveiled a show unit for its latest residential project, Residensi Mutiara, in conjunction with UDA HomeXBites 2026 held here.
UDA Land (South) Sdn Bhd chief operating officer Norazim Shukor said the programme gave prospective buyers an opportunity to explore the homes' designs and features, as well as obtain information on unit options, homeownership packages and UDA's property projects in Johor.
He said 50 Residensi Mutiara units were being offered, comprising two- and three-storey freehold townhouses with built-up areas ranging from 1,259 to 3,627 square feet.
Norazim said the development, located in the strategic Bandar UDA Utama area, was priced from RM548,700 and featured three bedrooms with either two or four bathrooms.
"The development offers an exclusive concept and a modern community lifestyle, with practical designs and layouts, as well as 24-hour security.
"It is also close to several major routes, making it an ideal choice for Malaysians working in Singapore," he said in his speech at the Residensi Mutiara project launch ceremony here today.
Also present were Dewan Negara deputy president Senator Datuk Nur Jazlan Mohamed and state Unity, Heritage and Culture Committee chairman P. Pannir Selvam.
Norazim said UDA would continue to play its role as a developer that creates a harmonious, dynamic and liveable environment through an integrated approach combining residential development, entrepreneur engagement and community activities.
Meanwhile, Pannir Selvam said quality residential developments should encompass the well-being, comfort and harmony of the community.
In this regard, he said UDA's initiative to provide a suitable living environment and appropriate facilities was a positive step towards strengthening unity and fostering an inclusive society.
He said the organisation of UDA HomeXBites 2026 also demonstrated how property development could be complemented by activities that benefit the community.
"The combination of a property exhibition, food sales and various exciting activities makes this programme not only a platform to showcase UDA properties, but also an opportunity to provide meaningful experiences for visitors and their families," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Husband to be charged tomorrow with murder of MCBA officer
Article:
NILAI: A 37-year-old man suspected of murdering his wife, a Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) officer, at the KLIA Quarters on Oct 15 will be charged tomorrow.
Nilai police chief Superintendent Johari Yahya said the suspect would face a murder charge under Section 302 of the Penal Code at the Seremban magistrate's court tomorrow morning.
"Following instructions to charge, the suspect linked to the death of an MCBA officer earlier this month is expected to be charged tomorrow," he said when contacted today.
Norhazwani Ibrahim, 35, was reportedly found murdered at her home in the civil servants' residential quarters at about 7pm.
Her husband, who was recently released from prison for drug-related offences, surrendered at the Bandar Baru Salak Tinggi police station in Sepang, Selangor, shortly after the incident.
The suspected motive was a domestic dispute after Norhazwani sought a divorce, with the application reportedly filed while her husband was still in prison.
A post-mortem found that she died from neck compression. Stab wounds were also found on her abdomen and cheek.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Perak headmaster transferred amid probe into alleged inappropiate messages to student
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Perak Education Department is investigating allegations that a headmaster of a vernacular school sent inappropriate messages to a female Form Three student.
A post on Threads claimed that the headmaster had sent messages, including "I love you", to the student.
Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said she had directed the state Education Department to investigate the matter.
"The headmaster has been temporarily transferred to the Bagan Datuk district education office pending the outcome of the investigation," she said.
The post urged parents and the public in Teluk Intan to remain vigilant, and called on the relevant authorities to take the allegations seriously and ensure students' safety.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PH to contest Melaka polls as one team, says Fadhlina
Article:
NIBONG TEBAL: Pakatan Harapan (PH) will contest the 16th Melaka state election as one team under its 'Melaka Rumah Kita' slogan, said Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek.
The PKR Wanita chief said the coalition remained committed to presenting its proposals to voters in the state.
"From the perspective of team dynamics and commitment, we remain Pakatan Harapan. We will go into the Melaka state election as one PH team," she told reporters after attending the Jelajah Negaraku: Aku Kasih Malaysia programme for the Nibong Tebal parliamentary constituency at Taman Widuri today.
Fadhlina, who is also education minister, said the 'Melaka Rumah Kita' slogan was part of the coalition's approach to engaging voters and offering an agenda aligned with the aspirations of Melakans.
She said greater participation by women in politics was among the key areas being highlighted ahead of the polls.
"PKR is fielding 30 per cent women candidates this time, which I think is also a good offer for the people to consider, particularly in continuing to elevate women as candidates for the Melaka state legislative assembly," she said.
She said women should be given greater opportunities to participate in decision-making and state administration.
The Election Commission has set Oct 31 for nomination day, Nov 10 for early voting and Nov 14 as
polling day
for the 16th Melaka state election.
Pakatan Harapan chairman Datuk Seri
Anwar Ibrahim
last night unveiled the coalition's 21 candidates for the Nov 14 Melaka election, with former chief minister Adly Zahari set to defend Bukit Katil.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: SkyWorld deepens Penang push with Batu Kawan expansion
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: SkyWorld Development Bhd is expanding its presence in Penang with the soft opening of SkyWorld Gallery @ Bandar Cassia in Batu Kawan, marking another milestone in the property developer's expansion in the northern region.
The new gallery follows the opening of its first Penang sales gallery in Seberang Jaya earlier this year and reinforces the developer's commitment to delivering quality homes to more communities.
SkyWorld said the gallery reflects its brand purpose, "Make Living Better", through thoughtfully designed homes that prioritise quality, innovation and improved living experiences.
Chief executive officer Lee Chee Seng said the expansion would be supported by innovative construction methods, including prefabricated prefinished volumetric construction (PPVC), to improve building quality and efficiency.
"As we continue to expand our presence in Penang, we remain committed to delivering quality homes through innovation, including the adoption of prefabricated prefinished volumetric construction (PPVC) technology to enhance construction precision, quality and efficiency, " he said.
SkyWorld will adopt PPVC for its Batu Kawan development. The method involves manufacturing building modules in a controlled factory environment before transporting them to the construction site for assembly.
Lee said the approach could improve construction precision and consistency, enhancing workmanship quality while increasing efficiency.
In August, SkyWorld said it was targeting new launches with a combined gross development value (GDV) of more than RM2 billion for the financial year 2027 (FY27).
The planned launches are expected to broaden its portfolio of revenue-generating developments while keeping the company on track to achieve its post-initial public offering target of RM4.6 billion in cumulative launches by the end of 2026.
SkyWorld's net profit surged 84.3 per cent year-on-year to RM5.3 million in the first quarter ended June 30, 2026, driven by higher contributions from its ongoing property developments.
Revenue rose 45.7 per cent to RM108.7 million, supported by progressive revenue recognition from a broader base of five ongoing developments, while gross profit increased 17.1 per cent to RM31.6 million.
On the stock market, SkyWorld shares have fallen 32 per cent from their high of 50 sen to close at 34 sen on Friday, a decline of 16 sen year-to-date.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Billion-ringgit investments alone do not define progress, says Sultan of Selangor
Article:
KLANG: A state's progress should not be measured solely by billion-ringgit investments, rapid development or high gross domestic product (GDP), but by whether its people benefit from its wealth, said Sultan of Selangor Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah.
He said there was little value in a state amassing great wealth if its people continued to struggle.
"True progress is achieved when the wealth generated by the state can be enjoyed by all its people. In a developed and wealthy state, the people, especially the poor and underprivileged, should benefit from that prosperity.
"The people should be provided with quality education, affordable housing and ample job opportunities, while being able to enjoy a clean and healthy environment.
"What must be emphasised is that the people should never feel forgotten by the government in its pursuit of rapid development," he said.
He was speaking at the investiture ceremony for the appointment and swearing-in of members of the Selangor Royal Court and royal dignitaries, as well as the conferment of Selangor state honours, at Istana Alam Shah here today.
Sultan Sharafuddin urged the state government to work hard to achieve success and progress across all sectors.
"I want to see Selangor remain progressive and competitive, with a high level of modernisation and an educated and accomplished population, while continuing to uphold religious values, good manners and humanity," he said.
The Sultan also said being a ruler was not a position of prestige to be proud of, but a trust and responsibility entrusted by Allah to safeguard the welfare and prosperity of Selangor's people and preserve the sanctity and dignity of Islam.
He recalled the pledge he made during his installation and coronation as Sultan on March 8, 2003, to uphold the sanctity of Islam and govern Selangor fairly, justly and honestly for the well-being of its people, in accordance with the Selangor Constitution of 1959.
"I take this opportunity to renew my pledge to continue safeguarding the sanctity of Islam and governing with fairness, honesty and responsibility for the prosperity of our beloved Selangor and its people," he said.
Sultan Sharafuddin also thanked Selangor residents for their continued support, prayers for him and his family, and trust in his leadership.
"I do not regard these 25 years as a personal achievement, but as a trust and a service to the people that I must fulfil. As long as Allah grants me the strength and opportunity, I will continue to discharge this responsibility to the best of my ability.
"I promise to continue protecting the people, safeguarding the religion and defending Selangor against any threats," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: FT008 detour near Gua Musang now open to light traffic after sinkhole
Article:
GUA MUSANG, Oct 25 — A temporary detour at FT008 Section 205.556 along the Gua Musang-Kota Bharu road near the Kesedar Ethnobotanical Recreation Park here was opened to light vehicles at noon today.
In a statement, the Gua Musang Public Works Department (JKR) said the detour, built using a Bailey bridge, was constructed at the site of a sinkhole on the road.
The detour, which is part of the Central Spine Road (LTU) Project Packages 3B and 3C, is open only to light vehicles.
Road users have been advised to follow temporary traffic signs and safety instructions, reduce their speed and exercise caution when passing through the area.
They should also plan their journeys in advance, while heavy vehicles are advised to use alternative routes.
The FT008 federal road near Kesedar Ethnobotanical Recreation Park was closed on Oct 10 following the formation of a sinkhole about eight metres deep. — Bernama

Title: Takiyuddin: Bersatu invited to PN talks on RoS case, Melaka polls
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Oct 25 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) will discuss its legal challenge against the Registrar of Societies (RoS) over the coalition’s suspension, as well as preparations for the Melaka state election, at a meeting in Kuala Lumpur tonight.
According to
News Straits Times
(NST), PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said Bersatu leaders had been invited to attend the meeting at PAS headquarters, but whether they would do so was up to them.
He said the allocation of the seven seats assigned to PN for the Melaka polls would also be discussed.
According to Takiyuddin, the seats will be distributed among the coalition’s component parties, with Bersatu excluded after deciding to contest under its own logo.
He said the limited number of seats available meant PN would need to work out a suitable distribution among the parties involved.

Title: IGP orders immediate CID probe into Noorizwan’s death in custody
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 25 — Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail has directed the Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department (CID) to conduct an immediate investigation into the death of Noorizwan Zulkefly, who died while in police custody at the Cheras District Police Headquarters (IPD).
He said the investigation must be conducted thoroughly following the discovery of several unusual injuries on Noorizwan’s body that warranted further scrutiny.
“I have asked the CID, particularly its director Datuk M. Kumar, to investigate this case as soon as possible and make the findings of the investigation known to the public.
“At the same time, once we receive the post-mortem report from the hospital stating the cause of death, we will issue an official statement on the next course of action,” he told reporters after the 26th convocation ceremony of Spectrum International University College (SIUC) here today.
Mohd Khalid said the Integrity and Standards Compliance Department (JIPS), which is responsible for investigating deaths in custody classified as sudden death reports, had issued a statement on the case.
However, police were still awaiting the laboratory report to determine the actual cause of Noorizwan’s death, he added.
Earlier, Bukit Aman JIPS director Datuk Aida Abdul Hamid was reported as saying that the post-mortem found no injuries to Noorizwan’s internal organs, with forensic examination identifying only external injuries on his body.
Noorizwan, 42, died on October 1 after reportedly being brought from the Cheras District Police Headquarters to Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz in Cheras the previous day. — Bernama

Title: Melaka state polls: PKR’s 30pc women candidates offer voters a more inclusive choice, says Fadhlina
Article:
NIBONG TEBAL, Oct 25 — PKR’s move to field 30 per cent women candidates in the Melaka state election is part of the party’s strategy to offer voters a more inclusive choice, said Wanita PKR chief Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek.
She said fielding more women candidates could also strengthen women’s representation in state politics.
“I think this is also a good offering for the people to make their choice, particularly in our efforts to continue elevating women as candidates for the Melaka State Legislative Assembly,” she told reporters after officiating at the Nibong Tebal parliamentary constituency-level Jelajah Negaraku: Aku Kasih Malaysia programme here today.
Fadhlina, who is also Education Minister, said that Pakatan Harapan (PH) had also launched the slogan “Melaka Rumah Kita” (Melaka, Our Home) as part of the coalition’s approach to contesting the election.
Yesterday, PH chairman and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced 21 candidates to contest in the Melaka state election.
The Election Commission has set October 31 for nomination day, November 10 for early voting and November 14 as polling day for the 16th Melaka State Election. — Bernama

Title: A split second, a lifetime of loss: Family recalls fatal Paya Terubong landslide
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Oct 25 — A 73-year-old doctor was killed when a landslide struck his family's home in Taman Seri Rambai, Paya Terubong, trapping him beneath collapsed concrete.
The victim, identified as Wong Kar Lin, died when a landslide hit the family’s residence at about 8.36am, trapping him beneath rubble in the kitchen while other family members managed to flee.
Speaking at the scene, Wong’s mother-in-law, Wong Poh Lim, who is in her 80s, recalled the terrifying moments leading up to the incident,
Berita Harian
(BH) reported
She said she had been taking a shower in an upstairs bathroom when her daughter, Chang Mei Nuo, 68, alerted her to the landslide.
“We were shocked and immediately ran outside to save ourselves. Everything happened so quickly,” she told BH.
However, by the time they reached the ground floor, they discovered that Wong had already been pinned beneath collapsed concrete.
Poh Lim said only the three of them were at home when the landslide occurred, while the couple’s four children live elsewhere.
She described Wong as a devoted son-in-law, adding that his loss was especially painful after more than 30 years together under the same roof.
Although both she and her daughter escaped unhurt, she said she remained deeply shaken by the tragedy.
For Chang, the loss of her husband was difficult to put into words. She said she was nevertheless relieved that rescuers managed to recover Wong's body intact from beneath the rubble.
Fire and Rescue Department personnel retrieved Wong’s body at about 11.21am, nearly three hours after the landslide struck.

Title: Malaysian hiker rescued after falling into 10m-deep hole in Da Lat, Vietnam
Article:
LAM DONG (Vietnam), Oct 25 — A 40-year-old Malaysian woman was rescued after falling into a 10m-deep hole while hiking in Da Lat, Lam Dong, today, the Vietnam News Agency (VNA) reported, citing local authorities.
The incident occurred at around 5.45am in the Hon Bo mountain area of Lam Vien–Da Lat ward, when the woman, identified by her initials G.S.W., was hiking in the area and fell into a hole, said to be part of an abandoned mining site, about 70cm in diameter.
She became trapped inside the hole; the others in the hiking group tried to pull her out but to no avail. Local authorities were called and decided to launch an emergency rescue operation.
Lam Vien–Da Lat ward coordinated with local forces and the Fire Prevention, Firefighting and Rescue Police Division under the provincial Department of Public Security to aid the tourist.
Rescuers successfully brought the woman out of the hole at around 7.15am and took her to Lam Dong General Hospital for emergency treatment.
Initial information indicated that she had sustained an injury to her right ankle. She received first aid before being transferred to the hospital for further treatment.
Hon Bo Mountain, near Thai Phien flower village in Da Lat, is a popular destination for hiking, cloud hunting and photography, attracting both local residents and tourists.
The mountain offers scenic views towards Da Lat’s centre, particularly in the early morning. However, spontaneous hiking and sightseeing in the area can pose safety risks, especially for visitors unfamiliar with the local terrain.
Authorities have advised that visitors exercise caution when exploring mountainous areas and avoid hiking independently in locations where the terrain and potential hazards are unfamiliar. — Bernama-VNA

Title: Melaka cafe gig death: Police reclassify case as murder after delivery rider dies; 10 detained
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 25 — Police have reclassified the death of a delivery rider who was seriously injured while attending a gig at a cafe in Kampung Jawa here on October 17 as a murder case under Section 302 of the Penal Code.
Melaka Tengah police chief ACP Halim Abas said the case was initially investigated under Section 326 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing grievous hurt using a weapon or dangerous object.
“On Oct 17, the victim, a 21-year-old man, was seriously injured while at the cafe to watch a gig. He was later taken to Melaka Hospital for treatment before being placed in intensive care.
“The victim, however, was pronounced dead at 3.53pm on October 21 due to serious injuries to the back of the head in the incident,” he said in a statement here today.
He said police detained 10 individuals aged 18 to 25 on October 18 and 19 to assist in their investigations.
The gig reportedly did not have a permit from the police or local authorities, and investigations into how the event was organised are ongoing.
Previously, claims of a death during a gig at a cafe in Kampung Jawa went viral on social media platform Threads. — Bernama

Title: Fadhlina says RM2,500 allowance for Form Six students to begin in first semester next year
Article:
NIBONG TEBAL, Oct 25 — Form Six students will receive RM2,500 in living allowances starting from the first semester next year, said Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek.
She said the allowances, announced under Budget 2027, would be disbursed after the registration process for all Form Six students had been completed.
“Once the registration process for all Form Six students is completed, we will disburse the assistance in their first semester,” she told reporters after officiating at the Nibong Tebal parliamentary constituency-level ‘Jelajah Negaraku: Aku Kasih Malaysia’ programme here today.
She said the allowance would be distributed in stages over the three semesters of study, with approximately RM800 allocated for each semester.
Fadhlina said the initiative demonstrated the government’s commitment to supporting the needs of Form Six students, particularly in their studies, while also improving the quality of Sijil Tinggi Persekolahan Malaysia (STPM).
Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, when tabling Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat on Oct 9, announced that the government had agreed to provide Form Six students with RM2,500 in living allowances.
The amount is equivalent to the allowance received by matriculation students and is expected to benefit 90,000 Form Six students nationwide.
The provision of the allowance was one of 12 resolutions raised at the Madani Pre-University Congress held in Klang, Selangor, last August. — Bernama

Title: Trade Ministry puts the squeeze on uncertified squishy toys, seizes over 5,800 nationwide
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 25 — The Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) seized 5,801 squishy toys worth RM70,428 nationwide for failing to display the required Safety Compliance Mark.
KPDN Enforcement director-general Datuk Azman Adam said the seizures stemmed from 15 enforcement actions during a Special Inspection on Squishy Toys conducted from October 1 to 14 to ensure compliance with child toy safety standards.
“A total of 1,845 premises were inspected, involving manufacturers, importers, wholesalers and retailers.
“KPDN views child toy safety seriously and will not compromise with any party that fails to comply with regulations under the Consumer Protection Act 1999 (Act 599),” he said in a statement today.
He also advised the public, particularly parents, to always check labels and safety compliance marks before buying toys for their children.
Consumers with information on the sale of suspicious toys can lodge complaints via WhatsApp at 019-848 8000 or 019-279 4317; the KPDN e-Aduan portal at e-aduan.kpdn.gov.my; the KPDN Call Centre at 1-800-886-800; or the Ez ADU KPDN smartphone app.
On a separate case, he said a trader was fined RM1,000 by the Putrajaya Magistrates’ Court last Thursday after pleading guilty to making a misleading representation in an advertisement.
He said KPDN had received a complaint from a customer, who had received a jubah instead of a baju kurung as advertised.
“Following the incident on February 27, 2024, an investigation was carried out, which led to the individual’s prosecution in court,” he said.
He said the accused was charged under Section 10(1)(a) of the Consumer Protection Act 1999 [Act 599] and was liable to be punished under Section 25(1)(b) of the same Act. The trader paid the fine. — Bernama

Title: Grandparents, two grandchildren among four killed after Ford hits stranded tow truck on PLUS near Yong Peng
Article:
BATU PAHAT, Oct 25 — Police have confirmed the identities of four people, including two children, who were killed in a three-vehicle accident at KM107 of the North-South Expressway (southbound), near Yong Peng, yesterday.
Batu Pahat police chief ACP Shahrulanuar Mushaddat Abdullah Sani said the 5.50pm incident involved a Ford Ranger, a Toyota Vios and a Scania tow truck.
He said the four victims were passengers in the four-wheel-drive vehicle. They were Ab Shukor Athan, 68, and his wife, Mariam Ibrahim, 65, of Taman Sri Lalang Baru, Kluang, and their two grandchildren, Nur Umie Zahiyah Jumie, 5, and her brother Muhammad Zaharil Hakimie, 1, of Taman Mutiara Rini, Skudai.
“Ab Shukor, Mariam and Nur Umie Zahiyah were pronounced dead at the scene by medical personnel from the Yong Peng Health Clinic due to severe head injuries.
“Muhammad Zaharil Hakimie died while receiving treatment at the Parit Yaani Health Clinic,” he said in a statement today.
Shahrulanuar said the accident also left four other occupants of the Ford Ranger with severe head injuries, including its driver, Jumie Julong, 35; his wife, Nor Hakimah Zakiah Ab Shukor, 32; and their son, Muhammad Zafrul Hakimie, 3, who are currently receiving treatment in the Yellow Zone of Sultanah Nora Ismail Hospital (HSNI) in Batu Pahat.
The couple’s other son, Muhammad Zariff Hakimie, 2, who sustained severe head injuries, is being treated in the Red Zone of HSNI.
He said the two occupants of the Toyota Vios - its driver, Chin Nyet Boon, 46, and Yong Ah Moi, 81, from Taman Meranti, Bahau, Negeri Sembilan - were also receiving treatment in the Yellow Zone of HSNI for head injuries, while the lorry driver, Mohd Nadzri Abd Wahab, 31, was uninjured.
Recounting the sequence of events, Shahrulanuar said preliminary investigations found that the driver of the southbound Ford Ranger was believed to have lost control of the vehicle while travelling in the left lane along a straight stretch of road before crashing into the rear right side of the lorry, which had stopped on the emergency lane due to engine trouble.
“The impact caused the Ford Ranger to spin before it was hit by the Toyota Vios travelling behind it.
“All the victims’ bodies were taken to the Forensic Medicine Unit of HSNI for post-mortem examinations, and the case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Loke announces RM1,000 payout for Melaka taxi drivers ahead of state polls
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Oct 25 — Transport Minister Anthony Loke today said taxi drivers in Melaka will receive RM1,000 in assistance on Monday, with the aid funded through proceeds from the sale of special “H” vehicle registration numbers.
Speaking at Pakatan Harapan's (PH) candidate announcement event in Melaka last night, the DAP secretary-general said the assistance formed part of the federal government's efforts to direct public funds towards initiatives that benefit ordinary Malaysians.
“To the taxi drivers in Melaka, I will distribute the RM1,000 to you on Monday,” Loke said, according to the
New Straits Times
(NST).
Loke said the payment would be funded through proceeds from the sale of special “H” vehicle registration numbers, which raised RM91 million.
He said the aid demonstrated how government revenue could be redirected to benefit the public, adding that Putrajaya remained committed to targeted assistance programmes aimed at easing cost-of-living pressures.
