Separately, Loke said Pakatan Harapan remained upbeat about its prospects in the Melaka election despite its recent setback in Negri Sembilan.

Title: Singapore consulate in Kuching to be located within Kuching South City Council area, says mayor
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 25 — The much-anticipated Consulate-General of Singapore in Kuching will be located within the Kuching South City Council’s (MBKS) jurisdiction, according to Kuching South Mayor Datuk Wee Hong Seng.
He said the location is likely to be in an area that has recently gained popularity among locals, in the vicinity of high-end residential neighbourhoods.
“More details will soon be publicly announced,” he said during his Facebook live session ‘Shall WEE Talk’ on Saturday.
He made the disclosure in response to netizens’ enquiries about the potential location of the consulate.
Wee went on to provide a few clues on the location, saying it is now a popular area, features high-end residential properties, and that its name contains the word ‘bank’.
However, he did not reveal the precise location.
It is noted that the plan to establish a Consulate-General of Singapore in Kuching was first proposed in 2023.
The proposal was highlighted when Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg attended the 10th Malaysia-Singapore Leaders’ Retreat held in Singapore, where he agreed to the establishment of the consulate.
Abang Johari pointed out that the consulate would help further strengthen bilateral ties and foster cooperation between Sarawak and Singapore in sectors including economy and tourism.
During a courtesy call on Abang Johari in January this year, High Commissioner of Singapore to Malaysia Vanu Gopala Menon announced that Singapore intended to set up consulates in both Kuching and Kota Kinabalu to enhance connections in trade, investment and tourism.
Vanu said the Singaporean Government had approved the plan by November 2023.
Following this approval, Singapore has been identifying suitable premises in Kuching and Kota Kinabalu, including the possible use of temporary office space during the initial phase. — The Borneo Post

Title: Driver killed after 4WD, car collide in Penampang, police appeal for information
Article:
PENAMPANG, Oct 25 — A 34-year-old man died following a two-vehicle collision along Jalan Datuk Panglima Banting last night.
Acting Penampang police chief ASP Arisanti Aziz said the incident, which occurred at about 8.30pm, involved a four-wheel-drive vehicle and a car.
Preliminary investigations revealed that the four-wheel drive, travelling from Bukit Padang, is believed to have lost control before colliding with the car driven by a 42-year-old man.
The 34-year-old driver was pronounced dead while receiving treatment at Queen Elizabeth Hospital I in Kota Kinabalu, while the car driver sustained minor injuries.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987, and witnesses or members of the public with information are urged to contact investigating officer Inspector Saparia Ladoni at 019-8095133 to assist with the probe. — Daily Express

Title: Sultan of Selangor: Criticisms aimed at safeguarding people’s well-being, not interfering in govt affairs
Article:
KLANG, Oct 25 — The Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, has said that his views, criticisms and concerns on matters relating to the state administration are not intended to interfere in the affairs of the state government.
Instead, His Royal Highness said such matters were raised to ensure that the welfare and well-being of the people remained a top priority.
“I do not want the people to view my criticisms as a dispute or conflict between me and the government. Instead, I want every criticism to be seen as part of my responsibility to ensure that the state administration always looks after the interests of the people and the future of Selangor.
“However, what saddens me is that the criticisms or ‘titah’ (royal pronouncements), as they are referred to in royal parlance, have been misinterpreted by certain quarters and a handful of politicians, as though I intend to interfere in the affairs of the state government or practise absolute monarchy,” Sultan Sharafuddin said.
Sultan Sharafuddin said this at the ceremony for the proclamation of titles, oath-taking and pledging of allegiance by the Orang-Orang Besar Istana and Dato’ Diraja Selangor, as well as the conferment of Selangor state honours, in conjunction with the Silver Jubilee of His Royal Highness’s reign, held at the Balairung Seri of Istana Alam Shah here today.
Sultan Sharafuddin also stressed that he was fully conversant with the provisions of the law and understood the extent of his role and responsibilities under the system of constitutional monarchy and parliamentary democracy practised in the country and Selangor.
His Royal Highness also respects the provisions of the Selangor State Constitution 1959 and the relevant provisions of the Federal Constitution concerning his position and powers as Sultan.
“All this while, I have discharged my duties as ruler in accordance with the trust and responsibilities vested in me, and I believe that every party entrusted with responsibilities in the government has its respective duties, which must be respected and carried out with full integrity.
“To my government, I urge you to work hard to achieve success and progress in all fields. I want to see Selangor continue to develop as a progressive and competitive state with a high level of modernisation and a knowledgeable, accomplished population, while continuing to uphold religious values, good manners and humanity,” His Royal Highness said.
Sultan Sharafuddin said the measure of a state’s progress should not be based solely on billions of ringgit in investment, rapid development or high gross domestic product figures.
His Royal Highness said it was pointless for a state to possess great wealth if its people continued to struggle, as true progress meant ensuring that the benefits of the state’s wealth could be enjoyed by all its people.
“For example, in a developed and wealthy state, the people, especially the poor and underprivileged, should be able to benefit from and enjoy that wealth.
“The people should always be supported through access to quality education, affordable housing, ample employment opportunities, and a clean and healthy environment. What is important to emphasise is that the people must feel that they have not been forgotten by the government in its pursuit of rapid development,” Sultan Sharafuddin said.
Sultan Sharafuddin also described his reign, which began in 2001 as the Sultan of Selangor, following 33 years as the state’s Raja Muda, as a journey that had been far from short.
The Sultan said that throughout this period, His Royal Highness and the people of Selangor had faced various challenges and trials, while also witnessing rapid development and changes in the state. These experiences had taught him much and deepened his understanding of the true meaning of a ruler’s responsibilities.
During his reign, four Menteri Besar had served alongside Sultan Sharafuddin to lead the state government.
“In my view, being a Sultan is not a position or status to be proud of. Rather, it is a trust and responsibility bestowed by Allah to safeguard the well-being and prosperity of all the people living in Selangor, while preserving the sanctity and dignity of Islam.
“I still remember the oath I took during my installation and coronation ceremony as Sultan on March 8, 2003, in which I pledged to uphold the sanctity of Islam at all times and govern Selangor with fairness, impartiality and honesty for the well-being of the people, in accordance with the Selangor State Constitution 1959.
“I take this opportunity to reiterate and renew my pledge to continue upholding the sanctity of Islam and to govern with fairness, honesty and responsibility for the prosperity of the people and my beloved state of Selangor,” His Royal Highness said.
Sultan Sharafuddin also pledged to continue to fulfil his responsibility to uphold Islam as the religion of the state and ensure that it continued to be respected and practised by Muslims in Selangor without being questioned.
At the same time, His Royal Highness urged the people of Selangor to continue living in peace and respecting and understanding one another, given the state’s multiracial, multireligious and diverse population. Differences in race, religion and culture should not become reasons for hostility.
The Sultan also urged the people to exercise caution when discussing sensitive issues and not to misuse freedom of speech in ways that could offend the race, religion or beliefs of others, while continuing to respect one another.
“Freedom must be accompanied by responsibility. Differences of opinion must be accompanied by courtesy, and progress must go hand in hand with human values. I want Selangor to remain a peaceful and prosperous state where its people live in unity,” Sultan Sharafuddin said.
His Royal Highness also expressed gratitude to Allah for granting him the opportunity to fulfil this trust during his 25 years as Sultan. He thanked all the people of Selangor for their unwavering support, prayers for him and his family, and the confidence they had placed in him to rule the state throughout this period.
“I do not regard these 25 years as a personal achievement. Instead, I see them as a trust and a service to the people that I must fulfil. As long as Allah grants me the strength and opportunity, I will continue to discharge this trust to the best of my ability.
“I pledge to continue looking after the people, safeguarding the religion and protecting Selangor from any threats. May Allah continue to protect Selangor, grant well-being to all its people, and bless the state with lasting peace, prosperity and success,” Sultan Sharafuddin said. — Bernama

Title: MBPP halts condo and road projects near fatal Paya Terubong landslide site, orders fresh environmental study
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 25 — The Penang Island City Council (MBPP) has ordered an immediate halt to condominium construction and roadworks on a hillside near the site of a landslide that claimed a man’s life in Taman Seri Rambai, Paya Terubong, here today.
MBPP mayor Datuk A. Rajendran said the stop-work order was issued to facilitate further investigations into the incident.
“The road and condominium projects have been ongoing for more than a year, while slope stabilisation works are also being carried out in the area.
“So far, we have recommended that the occupants of six houses identified as potentially unsafe relocate temporarily to prevent any untoward incidents,” he told reporters at the scene today.
In the incident, which occurred at about 8.36am, Wong Kar Lin, 73, a doctor, was found trapped after a landslide struck his house. Rescuers recovered his body at about 11.20am.
The victim’s wife, Chang Mei Nuo, 68, and his mother-in-law, Wong Poh Lim, in her 80s, managed to escape shortly after the incident.
Meanwhile, State Infrastructure, Transport and Digital Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said slope stabilisation works were being carried out in the area, but some sections had yet to be completed when the landslide occurred.
He said the immediate priority was to ensure the safety of nearby residents while allowing the relevant authorities to investigate the cause of the incident.
“Unfortunately, the section that had yet to be completed was the one affected by the landslide. Further investigations are ongoing before more detailed information can be provided,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Court acquits retired Risda employee of six misappropriation charges involving RM15,350 in association funds
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU, Oct 25 — The Sessions Court here today discharged and acquitted a retired Rubber Industry Smallholders Development Authority (Risda) employee of six charges of misappropriating RM15,350 in association funds about 10 years ago.
Judge Azman Mustapha made the decision after finding that the prosecution had failed to establish a prima facie case against Mohd Amran Ghazali, 61, at the close of the defence case.
“I have considered the case against the accused and found that the money used by the accused was for Risda state (association) programmes, and this is consistent with the testimony of the 7th prosecution witness,” Azman said in his judgment.
The court also ordered the return of the accused’s earlier bail of RM6,000.
In 2021, Mohd Amran, then serving as an administrative assistant at the Terengganu Risda Office, was charged with six counts of misappropriating RM15,350 between 2016 and 2017.
Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) deputy public prosecutor Nur Amalina Najwa Mohd Ali appeared for the prosecution, while Mohd Amran was represented by lawyer Muhammad Abdul Rahman Ab Razak. — Bernama

Title: Body of doctor pulled from rubble, residents evacuated after Paya Terubong landslide
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 25 — The body of a man buried in a landslide at a two-storey semi-detached house in Taman Seri Rambai, Paya Terubong, here, was recovered by firefighters at 11.20am today.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Operations and Firefighting Division assistant director John Sagun Francis said the victim, Wong Kar Lin, 73, a doctor at a clinic, was pronounced dead by Health Ministry personnel.
“Firefighters, together with the Civil Defence Force, carried out a rescue operation to extricate the victim, who was buried under the debris, before recovering his body from beneath the concrete rubble.
“We cannot rule out the possibility that the incident was caused by continuous heavy rain since yesterday, which may have destabilised the soil. However, further investigations are still ongoing,” he told reporters at the scene.
The victim’s wife, Chang Mei Nuo, 68, and his mother-in-law, Wong Poh Lim, in her 80s, managed to escape shortly after the incident occurred.
John said the victim’s body was recovered intact, although he had sustained severe injuries. The body was sent to Penang Hospital.
Following the incident, residents of six nearby houses were ordered to evacuate as a safety precaution to mitigate the risk of further landslides.
He said firefighters were still conducting inspections and clearing debris at the site as of 12.35pm to ensure the area was safe.
“A district-level disaster meeting is scheduled to discuss follow-up action and the safety measures to be taken by the relevant authorities,” he said, adding that the cause of the incident remained under investigation. — Bernama

Title: Upside-down Jalur Gemilang in Melbourne: Sabah, Sarawak firmly behind Malaysia’s sovereignty, says Mustapha Sakmud
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 25 — The people of Sabah and Sarawak remain firmly committed to upholding Malaysia’s sovereignty and reject any provocation involving the disrespectful display of the Jalur Gemilang by irresponsible parties overseas, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Sabah and Sarawak) Datuk Mustapha Sakmud said.
He was responding to an incident involving a group of individuals from the ‘Sabah Sarawak Keluar Malaysia (SSKM) Australia’ organisation, who staged a demonstration and displayed the Jalur Gemilang upside down in Melbourne on October 24 in conjunction with United Nations Day.
“The actions of a group of Malaysians disrespecting the Jalur Gemilang overseas risk tarnishing the reputation of Malaysians studying and working in those countries.
“Disrespecting the symbol of national sovereignty does not reflect the courteous and respectful culture of the people of Sabah and Sarawak,” he said in a statement today.
Mustapha said that although the Madani Government guaranteed freedom of speech, the democratic right did not exempt anyone from the legal consequences of their actions.
He therefore encouraged the public to lodge formal police reports so that the authorities could investigate social media content showing the Jalur Gemilang displayed upside down in accordance with the applicable laws.
On the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63), Mustapha said demands related to the agreement, which were previously considered sensitive, were now being discussed transparently and had been elevated to a key national agenda.
He said formal negotiations under Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s administration over nearly four years had resolved 12 MA63 matters, while the interim special grant to Sabah had been increased to RM1.5 billion annually.
He added that negotiations on Sabah’s demand for 40 per cent of its net revenue continued, to reach a comprehensive settlement.
“The people can judge for themselves the results achieved through negotiations and concrete action, compared with such provocations,” he said. — Bernama

Title: One in 23 Malaysian women now face breast cancer risk, up from one in 27, says Nancy Shukri
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 25 — The risk of Malaysian women developing breast cancer has risen to one in 23, compared with one in 27 previously, says Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri.
She said that based on the Malaysian National Cancer Registry Report for 2012-2016 and 2017-2021, breast cancer remains the most common cancer among women in the country.
“More concerning, the National Health and Morbidity Survey (NHMS) 2023 found that 71 per cent of women aged 40 and above have never undergone a mammogram, while 46 per cent do not practise breast self-examination.
“This low screening rate complicates early detection efforts, even though the survival rate for patients detected at an early stage can reach 95 per cent,” she said at the Sarawak state-level Breast Cancer Awareness Month event here today.
Nancy said that to widen access to early breast cancer screening, the government, through the National Population and Family Development Board (LPPKN), has introduced the Mammogram Examination Subsidy Programme since 2007.
She said the programme was later strengthened and rebranded to WeCaRe, which encompasses awareness of breast and cervical cancer among women.
As of Sept 30, she said, 598,919 women in Malaysia have benefited from the programme, including 90,075 women in Sarawak, with 88 of them testing positive for cancer. — Bernama

Title: One dead as landslide hits Paya Terubong house, two escape, says Penang Fire Dept
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 25 — A man was confirmed dead after being buried in a landslide that affected a house in Taman Seri Rambai, Paya Terubong here today.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations John Sagun Francis said it received an emergency call at 8.36am and a team from the Paya Terubong Fire and Rescue Station was dispatched to the scene.
“Upon arrival, we found that the landslide had affected the back section of a house, and initial reports indicated that three people, believed to be occupants of the house, were involved in the incident.
“Two of them managed to save themselves, while the third was believed to be trapped and buried, before being confirmed dead at 9.10am by Health Ministry personnel at the scene,” he said in a statement today.
He said that as of 9.45am, firefighters were working to extricate the victim from under the rubble.
The operation involved seven firefighters, including a supervisor, as well as a Light Fire Rescue Tender (LFRT) and an Emergency Medical Rescue Service (EMRS) unit, with assistance from the police. — Bernama

Title: Sabah Cabinet discusses Tawau water supply disruption amid prolonged dry spell
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 25 — The water supply disruption in Tawau was raised at the Sabah Cabinet meeting last Wednesday to ensure immediate action is taken to help affected residents.
Sabah Youth Development, Sports Advancement and Creative Economy Minister Datuk Nizam Abu Bakar Titingan, who raised the matter, said dry weather and a prolonged lack of rain have affected raw water sources, disrupting treatment operations and distribution since last week.
“I raised this problem at the Cabinet meeting because I understand the difficulties faced by affected residents.
“Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor has also directed the Sabah Works and Utilities Ministry to have the Tawau Water Department (JANS) take proactive action.
“This includes intensifying water deliveries by tanker lorries to affected areas. Sabah Works and Utilities Minister Datuk Seri Dr Joachim Gunsalam has assured that the issue is being monitored and capacity mobilised to help affected residents,” he said in a statement here today.
Nizam said the Tawau Water Department’s latest data showed that operations at the Utara Water Treatment Plant remain affected due to raw water quality problems from Sungai Tawau.
“Although there has been rain, the rainfall in the catchment area is still insufficient to significantly raise the river level and allow water treatment operations to recover fully.
He said water deliveries will continue according to current operational capacity, with better coordination to ensure affected areas receive due attention.
Nizam said the water supply problem cannot be taken lightly as it involves the people’s basic needs and affects households on a daily basis.
“I will be in touch with the ministry and JANS to get the latest developments on the situation and ensure the needs of affected residents continue to be addressed,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Even as skies begin to clear, eateries say the haze has already hurt business
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 25 — With lunchtime approaching, Gerai Masakan Panas Che Daud in Taman Sri Rampai would normally be preparing for the midday crowd. But at 11.40am, stall owner Che Daud Che Isa had just one customer to attend to.
The 59-year-old said business had slowed since the haze began, with some customers choosing to pack their food and eat at home rather than sit down at his stall.
He estimated that customer numbers had fallen by about half, as worsening air quality appeared to discourage people from eating out.
“My stall is facing some problems now. Perhaps it is because of the haze and people are afraid to come out, so the number of customers has decreased.
“Some customers are also opting for takeaway. They do not want to eat at the stall and would rather take the food home. But even then, the numbers are not as high as before,” he told
Malay Mail
.
Che Daud’s experience reflects the challenges faced by eateries as the haze continues to affect air quality across the Klang Valley, with restaurant operators reporting fewer dine-in customers, falling sales and changes in dining habits.
Che Daud Che Isa, 59, said the ongoing haze has affected business at his food stall in Taman Sri Rampai, Kuala Lumpur, with customer numbers down by about half. — Picture by Muhammad Yusry
Despite the drop in foot traffic, some eateries continue to draw customers, although their regulars are increasingly opting for takeaway.
A restaurant worker about 200 metres from Che Daud’s stall, who asked not to be named, said those still dining in were often motorists who stopped for a meal while waiting for their cars to be serviced at nearby workshops.
At Warung Paman Sol restaurant in Taman Keramat, near the Jelatek LRT station, owner Solihin Faeez Mohd Shukri, 32, said daily income had fallen by between 20 and 25 per cent since the haze began.
While customers had not directly blamed the haze for staying away, he noticed that families who would normally dine in with their young children were increasingly sending one person to collect takeaway orders instead.
“There has definitely been a change in customer traffic,” he said, adding that takeaway and delivery orders had increased, although not significantly.
Solihin Faeez Mohd Shukri, 32, said he noticed that families who would normally dine in with their young children were increasingly sending one person to collect takeaway orders instead. — Picture by Muhammad Yusry
Solihin said he was keeping the restaurant’s operating arrangements unchanged for now, hoping the situation would improve soon.
But he was concerned that prolonged haze could have longer-term consequences for the restaurant business, as customers might become accustomed to ordering food for delivery rather than dining out.
“If it continues, I am worried that customer habits may change. Customers might become accustomed to using food delivery services and stop coming to restaurants to dine in,” he said.
In Shah Alam, the impact has also been felt at Miscusi Express in Seksyen 9, where Amir Habibur Rahman, 32, said sales had dropped by about 35 per cent in the past week compared with their usual level.
Amir said sales were initially largely unchanged, but the decline became more apparent about a week after the haze began.
He said fewer customers were coming in to eat, while those who did visit tended to look for indoor seating, an option his open-air establishment could not readily provide.
“There are also fewer people walking past the shop than usual,” he noted.
Although takeaway and delivery orders had remained steady, the loss of walk-in customers had affected overall sales.
Amir said he had no plans to change the shop’s operating hours, from noon to 10pm, as sales were usually strongest around lunchtime and in the afternoon.
Instead, the business was continuing to operate as usual while providing free face masks to customers who needed them.
The open-air setting had also meant more dust than usual, requiring the shop to be cleaned more frequently.
Amir was particularly concerned about the possibility of the haze dragging on for months, saying prolonged exposure could affect the health of both customers and workers.
“My hope is that the haze will not persist for too long, as some have predicted it could last until February next year.
“A lot of things have already been affected, and if the situation continues to threaten the health of our customers and employees, we may not be able to sustain the business," he said.
Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip previously told
Malay Mail
that the haze was expected to gradually subside next week following an anticipated change in wind direction.
During the North-east Monsoon, stronger north-easterly winds and more widespread rainfall were expected to help improve air quality, he said.

Title: Zahid: Malaysia reaffirms commitment to assist Indonesia in tackling transboundary haze
Article:
BAGAN DATUK, Oct 25 — Malaysia remains committed to its offer of assistance to Indonesia to address the transboundary haze affecting the country, said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
He said the commitment had been discussed at the Cabinet meeting last Friday to ensure that appropriate measures could be coordinated for the benefit of both countries.
Ahmad Zahid said the Indonesian government had deployed more than 16,000 personnel along with various aircraft and firefighting helicopters, but aerial operations were facing challenges due to poor visibility. There was also a lack of cloud formations suitable for cloud-seeding operations.
“So, we sympathise with their situation. However, we still hope that this problem can be resolved because it is causing neighbouring countries, particularly Malaysia, to suffer the adverse effects of the haze on health, especially among those with conditions related to allergies caused by the haze,” he said.
He told reporters this after officiating at the Bagan Datuk 2026 Sultan Nazrin Shah Bridge Run here today.
Ahmad Zahid said bilateral communication had already been initiated at the highest level with the Indonesian government leadership to discuss the current situation.
On today’s running event, he said it had attracted 1,700 local and international participants, including from Australia, Indonesia, Singapore, France, India, Nepal and Thailand.
“It is better (organised) this year, but as was the case last year, heavy rain fell right up until now.
“Next year, we will upgrade it to a full marathon. Hopefully, more people will take part, and we pray that there will be no rain at that time,” he said.
The event featured three categories, with the 5km run recording the highest participation of 759 runners (44.6 per cent), followed by the 21km category with 575 participants (33.8 per cent) and the 10km category with 366 participants (21.5 per cent). — Bernama

Title: Anwar congratulates Sultan of Selangor on silver jubilee of reign
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 25 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today extended his congratulations to the Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, in conjunction with the Silver Jubilee marking 25 years of His Royal Highness’s reign.
In a Facebook post, Anwar also prayed that Sultan Sharafuddin would continue to enjoy good health and well-being and continue to lead and protect the people of Selangor with fairness and justice.
“Extending my highest congratulations on the occasion of the Silver Jubilee marking 25 years of the reign of His Royal Highness Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah Alhaj Ibni Almarhum Sultan Salahuddin Abdul Aziz Shah Alhaj, Sultan and Yang Dipertuan of Selangor Darul Ehsan.
“May Allah Subhanahu Wa Ta’ala continue to grant His Royal Highness good health and lasting well-being, and may His Royal Highness remain steadfast in leading and protecting the people of Selangor with fairness and justice. Daulat Tuanku, Dirgahayu Tuanku,” he said. — Bernama

Title: ‘I have not resigned’: Ismail Lasim dismisses exit rumours, says focus is on Negeri Sembilan Budget 2027
Article:
SEREMBAN, Oct 25 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim has dismissed speculation that he is stepping down, insisting that his full attention remains on preparing the state’s 2027 Budget, which is expected to be tabled at the end of next month.
Responding to reports by a Chinese-language newspaper claiming he had signed a resignation letter, Ismail described the allegation as untrue.
“The report is not true. I have not resigned. I am fully focused on planning Budget 2027,” he told
Harian Metro
(HM) when contacted last night.
Ismail said the state government was currently concentrating on formulating a budget that would benefit Negeri Sembilan’s more than 1.2 million residents as well as nearly 6,000 state civil servants.
According to him, his schedule has been filled with meetings, stakeholder engagement sessions and reviews of proposals and feedback that will help shape the state’s financial plans.
“The state government wants 1.2 million residents and nearly 6,000 state civil servants to receive the best benefits and advantages from this budget,” he said.
Ismail, however, declined to elaborate further on speculation surrounding his position.

Title: Serian top of the haze chart at API 194 as of 10am as 12 areas turn unhealthy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 25 — Twelve areas recorded unhealthy air pollutant index (API) readings as of 10 am today, with Serian in Sarawak recording the highest reading at 194.
According to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, three other areas in Sarawak also recorded unhealthy readings, namely Kuching (188), Samarahan (182) and Sri Aman (159).
In Johor, five areas recorded unhealthy API readings, with Pasir Gudang and Batu Pahat registering 156 each, followed by Kluang (154), Larkin (151) and Kota Tinggi (102).
In Negeri Sembilan, Nilai and Seremban each recorded a reading of 151, while Paka in Terengganu registered 154.
A total of 45 areas nationwide recorded moderate API readings, while 11 areas recorded good readings.
API readings of zero to 50 indicate good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and readings above 300 hazardous. — Bernama

Title: MetMalaysia places Penang and northern states under continuous rain warning until Oct 26
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Oct 25 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) today issued a continuous rain warning at alert level for Perlis and Penang, as well as several districts in Kedah and Perak, with the advisory remaining in force until October 26.
Affected areas in Kedah include Langkawi, Kubang Pasu, Kota Setar, Pokok Sena, Pendang, Yan, Kuala Muda, Kulim and Bandar Baharu, while the warning in Perak covers Kerian, Selama, Larut Matang, Manjung, Perak Tengah, Bagan Datuk and Hilir Perak.
The department advised the public to stay updated on the latest weather conditions through its official website, the myCuaca mobile application and its official social media channels.
It also said members of the public may contact the MetMalaysia hotline at 1-300-22-1638 for further information.
The warning was updated at 9.45am today.

Title: Overnight downpour floods Penang neighbourhoods, leaving dozens of homes underwater
Article:
BUTTERWORTH, Oct 25 — Continuous heavy rain for several hours last night caused flash floods in several areas in Penang, inundating homes in Taman Cantek and Jalan Jelawat here.
In addition, several other areas in Bayan Lepas, Bayan Baru, Seberang Jaya, Ampang Jajar and Bukit Mertajam were also hit by flash floods, but no victims have been evacuated.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations John Sagun Francis said it received an emergency call at 12.24am before dispatching personnel to the scenes.
“The flash floods in Taman Cantek affected 20 houses, with water levels estimated at 0.3 metres (one foot). The flooding was believed to have been caused by heavy rain and rising water levels in a nearby drain.
“We monitored the situation until it was under control and the water began to recede before ending the operation at 1.10am,” he said in a statement today.
He said flooding was also reported along Jalan Jelawat in Seberang Jaya as well as nearby residential areas, with water levels estimated at 0.3 metres due to continuous heavy rain and rising water levels in nearby drains. — Bernama

Title: Reject politics of hatred and build Malaysia together, Anwar tells Melaka
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 25 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has urged the people of Melaka to reject politics of hatred based on race and religion, and instead strengthen unity as the foundation for national stability and progress.
Anwar, also Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman, said the history of the Melaka Malay Sultanate and the nation’s independence struggle proves that momentous success comes through cooperation among various quarters, and not the struggle of a single group.
“I emphasise this repeatedly because some quarters attempt to distort history by claiming that this country can only be saved through the victory of a single race.
“If our ancestors succeeded in building the Melaka Malay Sultanate into a great empire, we can do the same through peace, unity among all quarters, and sound development strategies,” he said.
He said this when addressing the candidate announcement and launch of the Melaka PH election machinery for the Melaka state election at the Hang Jebat Stadium grounds here today.
Also present were DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke, Amanah president Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu, PKR vice-president and PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari, and Melaka PH chairman Datuk Seri Adly Zahari.
Anwar said elections should serve as a platform to explain government achievements, policies, and future plans, rather than an arena to insult opponents or incite political hostility.
The government, he said, must be judged on its efforts to address bread-and-butter issues, including the cost of living, job opportunities, education, healthcare, and basic amenities.
Anwar stressed that strengthening unity does not mean sidelining the interests of the Malays and Bumiputeras, but that national development must be carried out through the cooperation of all races.
Melaka, he added, must continue to be developed through the active participation of the Malay, Chinese, and Indian communities to ensure the state prospers and secures a brighter future for the younger generation.
The Prime Minister cautioned that racial division could undermine the country’s drive to master emerging technologies, artificial intelligence (AI), and the digital economy, while stalling job creation and income growth.
Anwar said the government remains committed to rectifying administrative shortcomings and discharging the public trust responsibly, adding that peace and stability must be safeguarded for the nation’s well-being.
Touching on the Melaka state election, he urged voters to evaluate candidates based on their dedication and commitment to state development, while reminding the unveiled PH candidates to uphold the people’s trust and serve them diligently.
At the event, Anwar announced 21 candidates who will represent PH in the Melaka state election scheduled for Nov 14. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia condemns deadly attack on Jordan church, stands in solidarity with victims
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 25 — Malaysia has strongly condemned the deliberate attack on the Greek Orthodox Church of St. George in Hamoud village, Karak Governorate in the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan.
According to the Foreign Ministry, also known as Wisma Putra, the attack constituted a grave violation of the sanctity of religious sites and a heinous act of extremism that has no place in any society.
“Malaysia extends its deepest condolences to the Government and people of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan, and to the families of the victims of the extremist attack on the Greek Orthodox Church of St. George in Hamoud village, Karak Governorate,” it said in a statement on Sunday.
Wisma Putra said Malaysia reaffirmed its steadfast commitment, together with Jordan, to reject extremism in all its forms and manifestations, regardless of motive or justification.
Malaysia also reiterated its commitment to strengthening the close and longstanding bilateral relations between the two countries, including in defending the shared values of religious harmony and peaceful coexistence, it said.
Malaysia also expressed its solidarity with Jordan during this difficult time.
Anadolu Ajansi, citing the state news agency (Petra), reported on Saturday that the death toll from Friday’s attack on mourners attending a funeral at Hamoud Church in Jordan’s southern Karak Governorate rose to nine.
Following the incident, Jordanian Prime Minister Jafar Hassan ordered three days of nationwide mourning beginning Friday, October 23. — Bernama
